references.text: The original instruction to make the ephod with gold, blue and purple wool, crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen.
The breastpiece was also to be made from the same materials: gold, blue and purple wool, crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen.
The skilled women spun with their hands and brought what they had spun: blue and purple wool, crimson yarn, and fine linen.
Description of the craftsmen's skills in working with the same materials used for the ephod.
The breastpiece was made from the same materials as the ephod: gold, blue and purple wool, crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen.
The list of materials that the Israelites were to give as a gift offering, including blue, purple, and crimson wool and fine linen.
The instruction for the belt confirms that this accessory is also an integral part of the holy garments, with identical materials and workmanship.
The curtain shares the same sacred materials as the ephod, which theologically connects the priest's service with the entrance into God's presence.
Solomon's temple uses the same sacred materials as the tabernacle, showing continuity in God's requirements for worship throughout history.
The gate curtain uses the same materials as the ephod, symbolizing that the entrance to God's presence is just as holy as the priest himself.
The general instruction regarding materials for the holy garments forms the theological foundation for specific parts such as the ephod.
